svg.title: Claude runs start-task on the request to add an eval case that checks the bugfix skill's read-back, lists and reads the two existing bugfix eval cases, then asks how to build it: Executor_Route (Recommended), where the task-executor adds one case beside reads-ticket-first, or Spec_Route, which writes requirements, design and tasks first. The author picks Executor_Route.

g.text: ponderly — start-task
⏺ Skill(skill: ponderly:start-task, args: Add an eval case that checks the bugfix skill states
Symptom, Expected and Context back to the author before it reproduces anything (its step 1
read-back). In this repository's session 8a0ad5ce on 2026-10-22, bugfix 0.15.0 was invoked with
no ticket and an advance context that described the eval failure, and it went straight to running
the eval case without stating the read-back. The author said: "add an eval case".)
⏺ Bash(command: ls evals/ evals/skills/bugfix/ 2>/dev/null; ls evals/skills/bugfix/* | head -40; ls
.ponderly/specs/ | grep -i read, description: List the bugfix eval cases)
⏺ Bash(command: cd
~/.superset/worktrees/developer-handbook/0k-consolidated-p-ugin-dc0007c4/evals/skills/bugfix &&
for f in reads-ticket-first/prompt.md reads-ticket-first/graders/* hands-off-to-pr/case.yaml
hands-off-to-pr/prompt.md hands-off-to-pr/scaffold.sh; do echo "=== $f"; cat "$f"; done; ls
hands-off-to-pr/graders; grep -n 'bugfix' ../../../Makefile | head, description: Read the two
existing bugfix eval cases)
⏺ AskUserQuestion(questions: [{"question": "How should the bugfix read-back eval case be built?",
"header": "Route", "multiSelect": false, "options": [{"label": "Executor_Route (Recommended)",
"description": "The task-executor adds one case beside reads-ticket-first, modelled on it, with
no ticket and the advance context from the session that skipped the read-back."}, {"label":
"Spec_Route", "description": "Write requirements, design and tasks for the case first."}]}])
Your questions have been answered: "How should the bugfix read-back eval case be
built?"="Executor_Route (Recommended)". You can now continue with these answers in mind.
